text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today, continuing a recovery that's built up over the past week as oil prices have stabilized and ticked higher. US crude is trading around $89.62 a barrel and global crude near $92, putting the company in a better position than it was two weeks ago when prices were evidently lower — the stock had dropped 7.6% over that stretch. The rebound suggests investors are reassessing the energy sector as near-term supply concerns ease.

The broader context is mixed for oil markets: Russia's crude production has recovered after a diesel deal, which is adding supply and pushing global oil back toward surplus territory. At the same time, heating oil prices are up 59% from last winter, signaling real demand pressure in certain quarters. For a major producer like ConocoPhillips, steady crude prices in the $90 range support profitability, even if they're not pushing higher.
